why: MI-280 unit U12. Closes BL-20260908-DOCUMENT-INDEX-WRITE-STAMPS-A-FALSE-LAST-VERIFIED-ON-436-DOCS-AND-THE-GUARD-TELLS-YOU-TO-RUN-IT (open, high, Tier-1). Tier-1 tooling: scripts/ops/**, tests/**, docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json. No src/, no config/, no deploy/, no order path, no strategy config, no risk cap. NOT landing machinery — checked by importing check_pr_landing.py and printing all twelve entries; the only match is the `.github/pr-landing/*.json` glob, i.e. this declaration itself, which R12 excludes by construction. THE DEFECT: `document_index.py --write` set `last verified` to TODAY on every document in the repo. That field is what a session reads to decide whether a document can be trusted, so stamping it asserts a verification that provably did not happen — no session verifies 1054 documents — and it destroyed the signal in the one direction that cannot be recovered: a document last genuinely assessed in May became indistinguishable from one assessed today, with no record of which was which. ⚠️ AND THE GUARD PRESCRIBED IT, which made it a trap rather than a footgun: document-index-guard's R1 failure names ONE unregistered file and hands you a command whose diff is three orders of magnitude larger. MEASURED A/B, same starting tree (origin/main plus ONE new document), same command, only the writer swapped: SHIPPED 472 files changed with 425 differing ONLY by that date (CLAUDE.md, docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md among them — hierarchy levels 1, 2 and 6); THIS CHANGE 47 files changed with ZERO differing only by that date. The census is re-measured, not inherited — the row's figures were from 2026-09-08 at 417bd6b6. THE CHANGE: build_rows() CARRIES each document's existing date from its own header unless the assessment actually changed, and stamp_for() carries identically, so the INDEX ROW and the HEADER get the same date from one computation — R3 compares those two surfaces and a carry applied to only one would be the very defect R3 exists to catch. Four never-collapsed bases print every run (carried / assessment_changed / new / restamped), and a new --restamp keeps the deliberate re-verification path with help text saying in terms that running it asserts a human act; a test pins that the guard's remedy line does NOT mention it, because the original failure WAS a documented instruction followed correctly. ⚠️ THE ROW'S LITERAL CRITERION IS NOT WHAT WAS ACHIEVED, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: it asks for `git diff --name-only | wc -l` to return 2, and run from a fixed point re-stamped THE SAME DAY the SHIPPED writer returns 2 as well (measured, as arm A of a first A/B) because stamping `today` is idempotent within a day. That count cannot separate the defect from the fix; the date-only count can, and it is what is reported. ⚠️ THE RESIDUAL 47 ARE PRE-EXISTING DEBT THIS SURFACES RATHER THAN CAUSES and are FILED, NOT FOLDED IN: 39 committed DOCUMENT-INDEX.md rows say `live` where a fresh build_rows() computes `unknown`, and the guard PASSES on that tree because R3 compares a header to that same stale row — two stale surfaces agreeing reads as coherent. Filed as BL-20260912-THE-COMMITTED-DOCUMENT-INDEX-RECORDS-39-STATUSES-A-FRESH-RUN-DOES-NOT-REPRODUCE-AND-R3-CANNOT-SEE-IT, measured with main's OWN unmodified writer so it is not an artifact of this change. Flipping 39 documents from `live` to `unknown` is a real assertion about 39 documents and deserves a human read, not a ride in a tooling PR. VERIFICATION: 12 controls; 8 planted defects, 8 caught, positive control quiet on restore — including that `never` is CARRIED (overwriting it with today's date is the defect in its purest form) and that an UNREADABLE file is treated as unstamped rather than silently carrying a date nobody saw. check_document_index.py --self-test still passes its 13 planted rule cases and the guard is still OK on the live tree. One decorative assertion carrying an `or True` was removed from the suite during the mutation run. ⚠️ ONE PROCESS ERROR WORTH THE RECORD: while measuring I cleared the experiment's output with `git checkout -- .` and destroyed my own uncommitted source edit with it — the same class as the row itself, the blast radius of the obvious command being larger than it looks, and the same remedy: scope the path.
